newsitem.title: UK: Softs Outlook - Coffee seen pausing before next rise.
newsitem.headline: Softs Outlook - Coffee seen pausing before next rise.

text.p: Coffee futures are expected to pause this week after rising to their highest level since mid-March on fund and industry buying.
Traders said coffee could hold or step back slightly to correct and consolidate recent gains, but the longer-term trend remained intact.

"I doubt we have hit the top," a trader said. "We are coming into the Brazilian winter period, and everybody is jumpy. It takes just one frost report to support another 20-30 cents (per lb) in the market."

London's July robusta contract rallied from Tuesday's low of $1,685 a tonne to Friday's high of $1,793 on fund and roaster price-fixing, but scaled-up origin sales emerged to cap further gains, traders said.
Coffee would have to lure further fund buying to set the stage for more gains. "Otherwise, it could just hang around here or turn softer," another trader said.
Traders said July could struggle at a recent high at $1,820, but that level should eventually give way and clear the path towards the May 1996 peak of $1,905.
Fundamentals could provide the catalyst to power coffee higher.
Robustas are in ample supply, but traders noted a shortage of higher quality beans.
"There's probably not as much good quality robustas as people thought," a buyer said.
And while roasters had been rebuilding some of their dwindling stocks, many still had much price-fixing to do.
Last week saw a fresh round of retail price hikes in Europe, the second in a year, and traders said another series of increases was likely by August if current market strength persisted.
Cocoa and white sugar, by contrast, were expected to remain in the shadows.
Nearby white sugar futures were seen holding most of their recent gains even if producer sales emerged on New York's July contract above 10.90 cent per pound and depressed raws prices.
The gradual upturn in physical demand should keep London's August contract supported above $310.00 and cause spreads to widen across the board, traders said.

Traders were monitoring freight orders from south Brazil to gauge whether Cargill's hefty raw sugar delivery would find homes, which would remove supply earlier than anticpated and boost raw sugar futures prices. Traders said a lift in raw sugar should pull London higher.

In cocoa, traders expected more consolidation at higher levels until fresh fundamental news emerged. Although July rose to the highest level since April 29 on Friday, traders noted volume was low. They saw July holding a wide range between the April 9 low of 980 stg a tonne and the April 2 high of 1,065.
However, if July continued to linger near current levels and built a solid base, it could test the upside in coming weeks.
One fund trader said that if July resisted dipping below 980 in the near term, it could move up toward 1,100 in the next six to eight weeks on bullish seasonal patterns.
